name: Ohio

agency.name: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Oil and Gas Resources Management (DOGRM)

form.name: Application for a Permit (Form 1), with Restoration Plan (Form 4), a surveyor's plat and the Authority and Organization form (Form 9)
form.notes: Read all 18 items and the instructions of Form 1 (4 pages, pdftotext) and the 2-page Form 4 (restoration plan) and a 9-page 2015 checklist of required documents; Form 9, the plat and the Division's own permit page were not read (the agency's main site answers 404 from here). Types of permit: drill new well, convert, deepen, plug back, reopen, revise location, reissue; expedite option. Notarized. Fees $500 to $1,000 by township population, +$250 expedite, +$5,000 mandatory pooling. Since the RICS online system, permits are filed and paid online (per the Permit and Plug List's 'RICS Permit to ...' types), so the paper form may be the same fields entered online; not confirmed. Valid 24 months (12 in urbanized areas).

api_number.n: API_WELLNO in the grid and the map layer; county code plus well number also in the grid

permit_number.n: APPNO in the Permit and Plug List export (PR + year + sequence); some applications are listed twice

well_name.n: WELLNM in the grid; WELL_NM and WELL_NO in the map layer; Form 1 item 10

lease_name.n: Restoration Plan (Form 4) item 5 only; Form 1 and the grid have no lease column

operator_name.n: CONAME in the grid, CO_NAME in the layer; some rows are individuals, not companies

operator_id.n: OPNO in the Permit and Plug List export; Form 1 item 2 'Owner #'

operator_type.n: Form 1 does not ask; the Authority and Organization form (Form 9) was not read

bond.n: Bond must be on file (Surety Section) before filing; not a Form 1 field; 2015 checklist

county.n: NAME (county) and CNTY_APINO in the grid; WL_CNTY in the layer; township also given

district.n: No district on Form 1 or in the grid or layer

field_pool.n: Form 1 names a formation to be tested (item 11), not a field or pool

surface_latlon.n: WH_LAT83 and WH_LONG83 in the grid (21 of 22 rows filled); WH_LAT and WH_LONG in the layer

surface_plss.n: WH_SEC, WH_LOT, township and WH_FTCALLS footage calls in the export; Form 1 item 10

bottom_hole_loc.n: Layer BH_LAT and BH_LONG; grid BH_SEC and township (14 of 22); grid BH_X and BH_Y empty

lateral_path.n: Map service has Horizontal Line and Directional Lines layers; whether surveyed or straight not checked

elevation.n: ELEV_GR in the export (ELEV_TGT empty in the sample); the well card shows GL, DF and KB

surface_owner.n: Form 4 item 6 property owner and item 31 landowner copy; Form 1 item 12 State surface rights

well_type.n: PROP_WLTYPE in the export: oil and gas (OG_R) on 98.8% of new-well permits, else gas storage, test; Form 1 item 6

work_type.n: APP_TYP and APP_TYP_Description in the export: 35 types seen 2019 to 2026 (79 in the page's drop-down)

well_direction.n: SLANT in the map layer; Form 1 item 5 orientation; not a grid column

proposed_depth_md.n: PROP_TD in the export (MD or TVD not stated); Form 1 item 11 'Proposed Total Depth'

proposed_depth_tvd.n: Form 1 asks depth of base of target formation, not labeled TVD

lateral_length.n: Form 1 asks only whether the whole wellbore is inside the unit

target_formation.n: PROPOSEDFORMATIONS in the grid; ProposedFormation in the layer; Form 1 item 11

formation_tops.n: Well card lists as-drilled formation tops after completion; Form 1 asks no expected tops

casing_program.n: Well card casing record is as built; Form 1 item 17 asks the proposed program; not in grid

cement_program.n: Form 1 item 17: cement top (ft) and volume (sacks) by string; not in grid or card

pressure_control.n: No BOP or pressure-control item on Form 1 (item 7 is pressure maintenance for recovery)

h2s.n: No hydrogen sulfide item on Form 1

pit_waste.n: Form 4 item 20: haul fluids and fill pits, or steel tanks; not in grid

water.n: Form 1 item 13: water source, withdrawal rate, total volume, watershed; not in grid

fracture_plan.n: Form 1 item 17 yes/no 'hydraulic fracturing?' per casing string; item 13 volumes

spacing_unit.n: DU_ACRES in the export (22 of 22 in the sample); Form 1 items 8 and 11 (pooling, unit, acres)

spacing_exception.n: Form 1 item 11 wellbore outside unit needs affidavit; grid has a VARIANCE column, empty, undocumented

mineral_owner.n: Form 1 item 12 royalty owner list attached; owner names are individuals, not published

fee.n: Form 1 instructions give the fee scale; grid FEE_AMT and RUSH_AMT were 0 on all 22 sample rows

notice_hearing.n: Form 1 item 18 swears notices were given; item 8 mandatory pooling order; hearing not read

date_received.n: DT_APP_RECVD in the Permit and Plug List export

date_approved.n: DT_APP_ISSUED in the export (the Application Issued Date filter); the well card shows 'Permit Issued'

date_expires.n: No date field; Form 1 instructions fix validity at 24 months (12 in urbanized areas)

spud_date.n: Well card 'Date Commenced'; not in the grid or map layer

completion_date.n: Well card shows 'Date Total Depth Reached', not a completion date; Completions report not opened

status.n: WL_STATUS_DESC in the map layer; well card 'Status'; not a grid column

plat_image.n: Ohio-registered surveyor's plat required with Form 1; online availability not verified

form_image.n: Well card links a scanned PERMIT pdf; not opened, so unknown if it is the filed Form 1

completion_report.n: Form 8 is the completion record; the card links a scanned well card; not opened

logs.n: Well card lists log types and links scanned log images (older wells shown)

production_link.n: Well card has annual oil, gas and water production by year

sources.tested: Read 2026-11-01. GET answers 200 (ASP.NET + Telerik search form, 66 KB). The export button exists only on the result page, so the export must be posted with the view state of a result page (any window's; it reads the dates it is posted with): that is what the first research's 'export did not work' missed. The export is an old binary .xls (BIFF8 in an OLE2 file, 0.6 to 1.1 MB) with the 70 columns listed. A search of all of 2019 to 2026 reports exactly 1,000 rows and its export then fails: a window that reports 1,000 or more is split. The export lists some applications twice, identical in all 70 columns (68 of 540 rows in 2019, 78 of 353 in 2020, 27 of 429 in 2025), so each application is counted once by application number. The Permit-or-Plug filter splits permits from permits to plug (about 400 a year); the unfiltered 2025 export (827 rows) equals the Permit export (429) plus the Plug export (398). 35 application types seen 2019 to 2026. The server redirects about one request in three to https://ohiodnr.gov/ instead of answering, at every pace tried (8 to 45 seconds); the same request is answered after a pause.

sources.tested: Read 2026-11-01 (the 2019, 2020 and 2021 editions; no 2022 or later edition exists at that path: 404). Used as the independent check: the Permit list, each application counted once, gives 472 against 492 (2019), 275 against 285 (2020) and 368 against 371 (2021), and the Plug list 325 against 325 and 205 against 202; all permits 797 against 817 (2019) and 480 against 487 (2020). The report is a snapshot taken after each year, so applications later cancelled could account for the gap (not verified).

grade_reason: The Permit and Plug List is a free, live listing of every permit application with its issue date, receipt date, application type (35 seen since 2019), county, operator, proposed depth, formation, acres and coordinates, and its Export To Excel button returns the whole result in one file. Held to B, not A: the export is a form post with a view state (no API), capped at 1,000 rows a search, lists some applications twice, and the server redirects about one request in three; and the permit's well type is oil and gas on 99% of new-well permits, so oil is not told from gas. Updated 2026-11-01: a producer reads the export each week and counts within about 4 percent of ODNR's annual reports for 2019 to 2021; the first research's note that the export did not work came from posting it without a result page's view state.
producer_plan: Built: d11_nat_oh.py. GET the Permit and Plug List page (hidden view state and event validation, plus the server's own session cookie, kept in memory); POST the search with every hidden field as it came, the two date pickers in all three forms they use (text, ISO value and client-state JSON), the three empty boxes with their placeholder text, the Permit filter and the Search button; read 'Item 1 to 25 of N' for N; POST again with the result page's fields and the Export To Excel button. The reply is an old binary .xls, read through Kentucky's OLE2 reader (ole_stream, records and num_text in d11_nat_ky.py). Windows: a calendar year at a time on the first run (17 requests, 6 s apart, 232 s), the newest 15 months weekly (3 requests, 59 s); a window that reports 1,000 rows is split, and a week still capped fails. Each application counts once by application number. Seven columns are kept (issue date, type, its words, county, operator, well type, application number); addresses, phones, the company representative and the contact columns never leave the reader. 35 application types are written out in TYPES (a type not in it fails the run, and so does a plug code on the Permit list): new-well types are new for an oil and gas well, inj for a service well, other for solution mining; deepen, drill deeper, reopen and plug back to drill = redrill; plain plug back and convert = rework; revise location and every re-issue = amend. Fluid is null. A redirect to ohiodnr.gov is tried again after 45 s, four tries, then exit 2; the runner's limit for Ohio is 900 s.
privacy_notes: The export carries operator mailing addresses, phone numbers, a company representative, contact (PM_*) and emergency-contact phone columns; some operator names on small and plug records are individuals trading in their own name. The Form 4 and Form 1 name property and royalty owners, who are individuals. The producer keeps seven columns and publishes only entity operators, county and counts.
